newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebel landmine kills soldier in Sri Lanka's north.
newsitem.headline: Rebel landmine kills soldier in Sri Lanka's north.

text.p: Separatist Tamil guerrillas detonated a landmine under a truck carrying food to troops in the rebels' former northern Jaffna stronghold, killing a soldier and wounding four, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.
The explosion occurred at Urelu in the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo, on Thursday, a ministry statement said.
Jaffna, which was controlled by the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) for nearly a decade, was captured by government forces last year after a lengthy offensive.
The rebels, who have now set up their bases in the Wanni region south of the peninsula, continue to attack military targets in the peninsula.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
On Wednesday, the rebels ambushed an army patrol in Pulmoddai, 260 km (163 miles) northeast of Colombo, killing 23 soldiers, the Defence Ministry said.
The LTTE said in a statement on Friday that their military capability was made clearly evident by their recent attacks.
"The LTTE are trying to evict Sinhalese forces who are militarily occupying Tamil-inhabited lands," it said.

About 20,000 troops launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", through the Wanni region last month in an attempt to open a highway linking Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
